newsitem.title: UK: Brokers not yet convinced of Panamax recovery.
newsitem.headline: Brokers not yet convinced of Panamax recovery.

text.p: Despite the current forward momentum brokers maintained that the freight market is "not catching fire" for October Panamaxes in the Atlantic.

Brokers were not yet sure if November will prove to be a significantly better month for owners in this area but there were reports of a considerable build-up of chartering demand from the US Gulf/Atlantic.

The situation in the North Pacific is already moving strongly favour of owners with early tonnage and thus no more ballasters are likely to be seen proceeding from the east to the US Gulf in the near future, brokers said.
The BFI gained 10 points today to 1044, the first double figure rise seen since aug 14.

GRAIN - NSAC fixed the Docenave-relet Silvretta 75,100 dwt delivery US Gulf about Oct 22 trip Far East at a firmer $10,350 daily plus $140,000 bonus but failed on subjects. Modern tonnage of this type remains in good demand for Oct and Nov although the market is uneven.
The 1978-built Petropolis 60,970 dwt was rumoured fixed from US Gulf about Oct 22/23 to Spain at a modest rate.

But there were reports that $22.50 no combo was bid today for first half Nov for 52-54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan, 50 cents up on the rate reported fixed yesterday by Mosk with C.Yalikoy for the same position.

Continental were said to be closely working their Oct Panamax stem US Gulf/Aqaba. Toepfer have split their Oct US Gulf/Poland from Panamax to Handy-size and could already have fixed about 40,000 tonnes at close to $11.00. Cargill may adopt the same tactic with their stem from US Gulf/Continent option UK. The north Pacific grain market appears solid with Chinese, Pakistani and Iranian charterers all quoting Panamax enquiries.
There was a shortage of tonnage for the early position. Navarino 63,880 dwt and Capt G Tsangaris 61,349 dwt have been fixed in this area on subjects.
Handy-size grain news concerned Continental's fixture of 21,000 tonnes 53' Up River/E.Med at $18.50 and Andre with 25,000 wheat Rouen/Libya for prompt shipment at a firmer $16.00.

New business quoted today included Finagrain with 25,000 wheat Southampton/Tunisia for Oct 15/25, Romac 25/30,000 Dunkirk/Hodeidah prompt, Andre 25,000 Rouen/Port Sudan Oct 18/23, Italgrani 16-18,000 completing to 25,000 Thunder Bay-St Lawrence/Italy Oct/Nov
Toepfer quoted 1/1.2m cft grain Brazil/Continent Oct 19/25, and Dreyfus 50,000 meals Up River and Brazil to China for Oct/Nov.

MINERALS etc - Hanjin's fixture of Esplanade 141,000 dwt delivery Fos Nov 10/25 for 12-15 months at $10,000 daily compared unfavourably with a similar fixture of a sister vessel at $12,000 daily in the summer. But brokers reckoned that HMM's booking of Lowlands Trassey 163,554 dwt delivery Brazil end Nov trip far East at $15,750 daily plus $350,000 bonus represented a stronger trend in trip rates. Mega Brook 123,000 dwt is said to have been fixed on subs for ironore from Seven Islands to Antwerp D Kleimar may have covered 70,000 ironore Tubarao/Ghent.
There are reports that Korea Line have booked Anangel Splendour 161,000 dwt on subjects delivery Japan mid Oct for 2 laden legs trading at over $10,000 daily.

Panamax coal rates have continued to rise in the far East. North princess 71,200 dwt is understood to have obtained at least $8,000 daily from Mosk delivery Japan Oct 18/25 for an E. Australian round.
Bao Shan are said to have fixed Bunga Saga Tiga 72,338 dwt delivery Jakarta Triphina at $9,000 daily and K Line may have covered Australia/Japan coal on private terms.
In the Atlantic Ascension 61,440 dwt was rumoured fixed by Coeclerici with coal Maracaibo to Italy and Orlando 72,000 dwt with pigiron Vitoria/US Gulf by IMC but further details were lacking.
HANDY-SIZES - Albatross failed with Sincere Oceanus 38,030 dwt Continent/Far East at $10,350 daily but Pacific Carriers were said to have booked a 30,000 dwt vessel on this route.
Combac took a craned bulker of about 35,000 dwt from N. Continent to US Gulf at close to $6,500 daily. Otherwise market news was lacking in this section.
